title: Where Does a Spring Hide Energy? Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
Press the spring in a pen and it pushes back. Sit on a sofa and its springs push you up. A squeezed spring can do work, so it must be storing energy. Aarav loads his toy spring gun, pulls the trigger and the ball shoots across the room. Where was that energy hiding, and how much was there? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC students, plus JEE Main and NEET, we learn the potential energy of a spring.

An 8 kg block on a k = 200 N/m spring is pulled to 10 cm and 20 cm on a live simulation: the spring pulls back with 20 N and then 40 N (Hooke's law, F = -kx), and the shaded triangle under the force graph grows to 4 J. Then it is let go, and a slow-mo replay shows the force and U at zero and the speed largest in the middle. We derive U = ½kx² from the area under the F-x graph step by step, see link by link why double the stretch means four times the energy, compare a stretch with a squeeze, and find which of two springs stores more under the same pull. Then a worked example on the toy gun, the exam trap about kx times x, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

In this video:
